deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1983 axiomatics of a 'homotopy theory' A ↦ H(A), assigning to each small category A a category H(A), with inverse images f^*_H and adjoints f_!^H, f_*^H. This is a direct precursor of the 'dérivateurs' of Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs. The previous page lists Hyp 4–6 (base change for (co)fibrant squares; fully faithful functors; localisations). This page treats cofinality and the effect of adjunctions.

(1) Cofinality. For a functor i: A_0 → A the question is: when is the canonical map ∫_{A_0} i^*F → ∫_A F an isomorphism for every F in H(A)? Here ∫_A = p_!^H with p: A → e is the homotopy colimit. Grothendieck takes this as the definition of (homotopy) cofinality.

(2) Functors with an adjoint. Suppose i has a left adjoint j: A → A_0, with j ⊣ i. Grothendieck 'presumes' the boxed formula i^*_H ≅ j_!^H.
- Modern proof: A ↦ H(A) is a 2-functor, contravariant on 1-cells and covariant on 2-cells.
- Applying it to the unit id → ij and the counit ji → id gives an adjunction i^* ⊣ j^*.
- So i^* is a left adjoint of j^*, and by uniqueness of adjoints i^* ≅ j_!.

(3) Consequence. Let p_0: A_0 → e and p: A → e. Then p_{0!} i^* ≅ p_{0!} j_! ≅ (p_0 j)_! = p_!, because p_0 j = p. Hence a right adjoint (a functor with a left adjoint) is homotopy cofinal. The second formula, p_{0!} i_! ≅ p_!, is just functoriality, since p_0 i = p.

(4) Example. Take A_0 = point, sent to a final object e of A. The inclusion e: pt → A has the left adjoint A → pt, so ∫_A F ≅ F(e). This is the familiar fact that the homotopy colimit over a category with a final object is evaluation there.

(5) Left margin. A question whether ordinary cofinal functors, for filtering/cofiltering categories, are also cofinal in this homotopical sense.

(6) Footnote * (the 'commutative diagrams to be added', a proposed extra axiom or lemma). For an arbitrary j: A → B and Yoneda embeddings h_A: A → A^, h_B: B → B^, one has (h_B)_! j_! ≅ (j^*_∧)^* (h_A)_!. Here j^*_∧: B^ → A^ is restriction of presheaves. The proof uses (2) twice:
- the presheaf-level adjunction j_!^∧ ⊣ j^*_∧ gives (j^*_∧)^*_H ≅ (j_!^∧)_!^H;
- j_!^∧ h_A ≅ h_B j (left Kan extension of representables);
- so (h_B)_! j_! ≅ (j_!^∧ h_A)_! ≅ (j_!^∧)_!(h_A)_! ≅ (j^*_∧)^*(h_A)_!.
Thus any homotopy left Kan extension j_! is conjugated, via the Yoneda embeddings, into an inverse-image functor between (large) presheaf categories.

(7) NB. If j has a right adjoint i, then restriction along j equals left Kan extension along i on presheaves: j^*_∧ = i_!^∧. This restricts to i: B → A on representables, so (i_!^∧)^*_H 'induces' i^*_H, consistent with (2).

The next page goes on to a Mayer–Vietoris/gluing axiom for covers of A by a crible and a cocrible.
errors: No real errors. The 'presumed' boxed identity i^* = j_! for j ⊣ i is correct and follows formally from 2-functoriality, as Grothendieck himself later establishes in Les Dérivateurs.
The footnote diagram requires H to be defined on large categories (A^, B^) and requires (h_A)_! to exist. These set-theoretic issues are not addressed.
In the NB, 'induit' is loose: (i_!^∧)^* agrees with i^* only after composing with the Yoneda embeddings.

ideas.what: Define cofinality of i: A_0 → A by the homotopy-colimit comparison ∫_{A_0} i^*F ≅ ∫_A F for all F
ideas.modern_name: homotopy cofinal / homotopy final functor in a derivator
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bousfield–Kan (1972); Quillen Theorem A (1973); in derivator language Grothendieck, Heller, Cisinski
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks (asphérique functors) and Les Dérivateurs

ideas.what: If j ⊣ i then i^*_H ≅ j_!^H (and dually), by 2-functoriality of H
ideas.modern_name: adjunctions are preserved by a prederivator; u ⊣ v implies v^* ≅ u_!
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Les Dérivateurs), Heller (1988); standard in Groth's and Cisinski's expositions

ideas.what: Right adjoints are homotopy cofinal; hocolim over a category with final object is evaluation at it
ideas.modern_name: homotopy cofinality of right adjoints; colimit over category with terminal object

ideas.what: Compatibility of homotopy Kan extension j_! with Yoneda embeddings: (h_B)_! j_! ≅ (j^*)^*(h_A)_!, turning left Kan extensions into restrictions on presheaf categories
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda/presheaf-level comparison of homotopy Kan extensions (derivator extended to large presheaf categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; related ideas appear in Cisinski's work on derivators and presheaves

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes adding axioms or lemmas expressing H on large presheaf categories via Yoneda, so that homotopy left Kan extensions become inverse images along presheaf-level restriction functors. He did not carry this out here, and it is not a standard axiom of derivators.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor technical device. It anticipates the use of large 'free cocompletion' derivators of presheaves, but specialists would find it routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains standard derivator facts (adjunction lemma, cofinality of right adjoints, final-object example), recorded in an early 1983 state that later appears in Les Dérivateurs. The Yoneda-conjugation diagram is a small, apparently unpublished technical aside, but not significant.
transcription_corrections: '(j, j rept. des foncteurs adjoints)' probably reads '(i, j resp. des foncteurs adjoints)'; the second letter is likely i.

Left margin: probably 'Cas des catégories cofiltrantes [or filtrantes] ("Et filtrantes??") cofinales (ordinaires)'. The reading is uncertain, but it concerns whether ordinary cofinality implies homotopy cofinality.
'les formules sont, ici, évidentes' may read 'déduites'; above the formula line the word looks like 'déduites'.
The first displayed formula follows from p_0 j = p, not p_0 i = p; only the second formula p_{0!} i_! ≅ p_! is the consequence of p_0 i = p, as written.
